sources.agency: CAL FIRE / Office of the State Fire Marshal
sources.title: Fire Hazard Severity Zones
sources.notes: Three classifications (Moderate/High/Very High); SRA maps effective April 1, 2024; LRA 2025 rollout dates; 2026 SRA public comment period November 9, 2026 - January 8, 2027; hazard is not risk.

sources.title: Flood Maps
sources.notes: 1% or greater annual chance is high risk; at least one-in-four chance of flooding during a 30-year mortgage; Map Service Center is the official location for flood hazard mapping products.

sources.title: Flood Data Viewers and Geospatial Data / National Flood Hazard Layer
sources.notes: NFHL is the geospatial database of current effective flood hazard data; covers over 90% of the U.S. population; address search available in the NFHL viewer.

sources.title: Flood Insurance / National Flood Insurance Program
sources.notes: NFIP provides insurance to property owners, renters and businesses; typically a 30-day waiting period; flood damage is generally not covered by homeowners insurance.

sources.agency: California Geological Survey, Department of Conservation
sources.title: The California Seismic Hazards Program
sources.notes: Earthquake Zones of Required Investigation (Alquist-Priolo fault zones, liquefaction, earthquake-induced landslides, tsunami); sellers must disclose if a property lies in a mapped zone; EQ ZApp is the authoritative map application.

sources.title: FAQ — What is the probability that an earthquake will occur in the Los Angeles Area?
sources.notes: UCERF3 30-year probabilities for the Los Angeles region: 60% (M6.7), 46% (M7), 31% (M7.5).

sources.title: Sustainable Insurance Strategy — California Homeowners Insurance Market Snapshot

sources.title: Consumer Alert, May 1, 2026 — FAIR Plan growth slows
sources.notes: FAIR Plan added approximately 16,000 residential policies in Q1 2026 (about 2.4%); commercial policy counts 21,200 to 21,464.
